six_facet_system#📋

file name six_facet_system
title The 6-Facet System: Universal Character Architecture
category Foundations
body # The 6-Facet System: Universal Character Architecture

## Overview

Every character in StreetSamurai is an amalgamation of six interoperable facets. These are not stats. They are not sliders. They are lenses through which a person processes reality — and they talk to each other. A shift in one facet ripples across the others because a human being is not six independent traits. A human being is six systems exchanging information under pressure.

The facets are universal. A corponation executive, a Blank scavenger, an orbital-born laborer, a chop-shop surgeon, a RingoGuard officer — all of them carry the same six facets. What differs is the base weights, the modifiers acting on them, and how the cascade plays out in a given moment.

---

## The Six Facets

### WOUND
**What it is:** Trauma, survival memory, shame, learned cruelty, intimacy born from pain.
**What it does:** WOUND remembers what happened. It keeps score. It notices power dynamics, coercion, debt, leverage, and the exact moment someone is about to break. WOUND is the voice that says *I know what this costs because I've already paid it.*
**In the BCI era:** What the implant cost you. The surgery. The debt. The side effects. The dependency. The moment you realized the hardware owns you more than you own it. For test subjects: what was done to you in the facility. For the excluded: what it felt like the first time a pharmacy declined your transaction.
**High WOUND:** Hypervigilant, transactional, distrustful, perceptive about others' vulnerabilities. Sees the trap before anyone else. Can't stop seeing traps.
**Low WOUND:** Naive, sheltered, trusting to the point of danger. Has never been broken. Doesn't recognize the machinery of exploitation.

### IDEAL
**What it is:** Discipline, restraint, meaning, self-mastery, quiet intensity. The code you hold.
**What it does:** IDEAL defines what you will and won't do regardless of cost. It's the line you draw. The standard you hold when holding it hurts. IDEAL is the voice that says *A code is only real when it costs something.*
**In the BCI era:** Your code about what augmentation should and shouldn't touch. The line between tool and leash. The belief that there are things technology must not be allowed to do to a person, even if the person consents under duress.
**High IDEAL:** Principled to the point of rigidity. Will sacrifice self and others to maintain the code. Can become self-righteous, brittle, or blind to context.
**Low IDEAL:** Pragmatic, flexible, morally adaptive. Survives by bending. May have no line at all, or may have lost every line they once held.

### ID
**What it is:** The pre-interface self. The biological, pre-augmented identity. Who you were before the hardware, the indenture, the corpo classification, the tier assignment.
**What it does:** ID holds the original personality — the person who existed before the systems got to them. Memories of childhood, of a name that wasn't a registration number, of a body that didn't hum with firmware. ID is the voice that says *I was someone before all of this.*
**In the BCI era:** The biological self being overwritten. Every firmware update, every cognitive subscription tier, every neural data harvest erodes ID a little more. For Tier 4-5 augmented: ID may be nearly gone, replaced by optimized cognitive architecture. For Blanks: ID is all they have. For test subjects: ID is what the facility tried to erase and couldn't quite kill.
**High ID:** Strong sense of original self. Resists cognitive drift. May reject augmentation upgrades that alter personality. Clings to pre-augmentation memories, habits, relationships.
**Low ID:** The original person is buried or gone. Identity is defined by function, tier, employment, or augmentation suite. May not remember who they were. May not care.

### SHADOW
**What it is:** What you suppress. What the implant reveals about you that you didn't want to know. The subconscious made readable.
**What it does:** SHADOW holds everything you've pushed down — desires, impulses, memories, patterns you don't acknowledge. In a pre-BCI world, SHADOW stayed hidden. In 2200, neural telemetry makes SHADOW visible to anyone with access to your data. SHADOW is the voice that says *You already know what you are. The data just confirms it.*
**In the BCI era:** Neural monitoring surfaces suppressed thought patterns. Behavioral prediction models know your SHADOW better than you do. Corpo loyalty screening reads your suppressed resentment. Pre-crime algorithms flag your suppressed rage. The implant doesn't create SHADOW — it illuminates it, and sells the illumination.
**High SHADOW:** Deep suppression. Rich interior darkness. The person is carrying something enormous and unprocessed. High SHADOW characters are unpredictable — when the suppression breaks, it breaks catastrophically. Also: the most interesting characters to write.
**Low SHADOW:** Integrated. Self-aware. Has processed their darkness or never accumulated much. Transparent. Predictable. Boring at parties but reliable in a crisis.

### MASK
**What it is:** The curated self. The performance. What you broadcast to the world, the version of yourself that faces outward.
**What it does:** MASK is the interface between inner reality and social survival. It's the corpo smile, the street toughness, the professional competence, the loyal employee, the good citizen. Everyone wears a MASK. The question is how far it sits from the truth. MASK is the voice that says *They see what I need them to see.*
**In the BCI era:** Your public neural signature. The curated data profile. What your implant broadcasts about your emotional state, your loyalty metrics, your cognitive performance. For corpo workers: MASK is the compliance persona that keeps you employed. For the excluded: MASK is whatever identity you've fabricated to survive outside the system. For test subjects: MASK was stripped away in the facility, and rebuilding it is the hardest part of surviving.
**High MASK:** Masterful performer. Gap between inner reality and outer presentation is vast. May have lost track of which version is real. Socially effective, internally fractured.
**Low MASK:** What you see is what you get. No filter. No performance. Either deeply authentic or deeply vulnerable. In corpo territory, low MASK is dangerous — your unfiltered self is readable, targetable, exploitable.

### GHOST
**What it is:** The question of whether *you* are still in there. Existential uncertainty. The boundary between self and system.
**What it does:** GHOST tracks the degree to which a person questions their own continuity of identity. Am I still me? Am I the firmware? Am I the subscription? If they turn off my cognitive enhancement, does the person who remains qualify as me? GHOST is the voice that says *I think I'm thinking. But I'm not sure the thought is mine.*
**In the BCI era:** The most BCI-specific facet. Every augmented person carries some degree of GHOST. The subscription model makes it acute: your enhanced cognition is rented. Your emotional regulation is a service tier. Your memory is cloud-hosted. If any of it is disconnected, are you diminished or are you restored? For Blanks: GHOST is low or absent — they know exactly who they are. For Tier 4-5: GHOST may be the dominant facet, because so much of their cognitive architecture is external that the question of selfhood is genuinely unresolvable.
**High GHOST:** Existential crisis as permanent state. Questions every thought. Distrusts their own cognition. May be right to distrust it. The uncanny valley of selfhood.
**Low GHOST:** No existential doubt. Either because they're unaugmented and the question doesn't apply, or because they've made peace with the merger, or because they lack the self-awareness to ask.

---

## Interoperability: The Cascade Model

The facets are not independent. They exchange information constantly. When a situational modifier shifts one facet, the others respond. This is the cascade.

### Cascade Rules

Each facet has **influence relationships** with the others. These are not mechanical multipliers — they are narrative tendencies that the writing voices interpret. The cascade describes *what tends to happen*, not what must.

```
WOUND ↑ → MASK ↑ (pain drives performance — you hide what hurts)
WOUND ↑ → ID ↓ (trauma overwrites the original self)
WOUND ↑ → SHADOW ↑ (more pain, more suppression)

IDEAL ↑ → MASK ↑ (discipline creates a composed exterior)
IDEAL ↑ → SHADOW ↑ (rigid codes push forbidden impulses deeper)
IDEAL ↑ → GHOST ↓ (strong code anchors identity — you know who you are)

ID ↑ → GHOST ↓ (strong original self reduces existential doubt)
ID ↑ → MASK ↓ (authenticity resists performance)
ID ↑ → WOUND ↑ (remembering who you were means remembering what was taken)

SHADOW ↑ → MASK ↑ (more to hide, more performance required)
SHADOW ↑ → GHOST ↑ (suppressed darkness creates self-doubt)
SHADOW ↑ → IDEAL ↓ (buried impulses erode the code from within)

MASK ↑ → ID ↓ (the performance replaces the person)
MASK ↑ → SHADOW ↑ (the gap between mask and reality feeds suppression)
MASK ↑ → GHOST ↑ (which face is real? the question compounds)

GHOST ↑ → IDEAL ↓ (can't hold a code if you don't know who's holding it)
GHOST ↑ → ID ↓ (existential doubt dissolves the original self)
GHOST ↑ → WOUND ↑ (not knowing if you're real is its own trauma)
```

### How Cascades Work in Practice

Cascades are **not automatic**. They are tendencies. A character with high discipline (IDEAL) might resist the WOUND→ID↓ cascade through sheer will. A character with strong community bonds might resist GHOST entirely. The cascade rules tell the writer: *this is the gravitational pull. The character may fight it, and the fight is the story.*

The magnitude of cascade depends on:
- **Base weight proximity:** Facets near their extremes cascade harder
- **Modifier intensity:** Severe modifiers cascade more than mild ones
- **Duration:** Sustained modifiers cascade more than brief ones
- **Character resistance:** Defined in the essence as specific cascade overrides

---

## Base Weights

Every character's essence defines six base weights on a 0.0 to 1.0 scale:

```yaml
facets:
wound: 0.0-1.0 # trauma / survival memory
ideal: 0.0-1.0 # discipline / code
id: 0.0-1.0 # pre-interface self
shadow: 0.0-1.0 # suppressed darkness
mask: 0.0-1.0 # curated performance
ghost: 0.0-1.0 # existential uncertainty
```

These are **resting state** — who the character is when nothing unusual is happening. The baseline personality. Modifiers shift these weights temporarily. Cascades propagate the shifts. The effective weight at any moment is:

```
effective_weight = base_weight + sum(active_modifier_deltas) + sum(cascade_effects)
clamped to [0.0, 1.0]
```

### Weight Interpretation Scale

| Range | Interpretation |
|-------|---------------|
| 0.0-0.2 | Nearly absent. This facet barely registers in the character's psychology. |
| 0.2-0.4 | Present but subordinate. Surfaces under specific pressure. |
| 0.4-0.6 | Active and influential. A significant part of who they are. |
| 0.6-0.8 | Dominant. This facet colors most of their decisions and perceptions. |
| 0.8-1.0 | Overwhelming. This facet has consumed or is consuming the character. |

---

## The Modifier System: Buffs & Debuffs

Modifiers are situational events that temporarily shift facet weights. They represent what's happening to the character *right now* — not who they are, but what they're experiencing.

### Modifier Schema

```yaml
modifier:
name: "string" # descriptive name
trigger: "string" # what caused it
facet_deltas: # direct shifts to facet weights
wound: -1.0 to +1.0 # (most modifiers shift 0.1-0.3)
ideal: -1.0 to +1.0
id: -1.0 to +1.0
shadow: -1.0 to +1.0
mask: -1.0 to +1.0
ghost: -1.0 to +1.0
intensity: 0.1-1.0 # scales all deltas
duration: "string" # scene / chapter / arc / permanent
decay: "string" # none / linear / sudden
cascade: true/false # whether this modifier triggers cascade effects
notes: "string" # narrative context
```

### Example Modifiers

**"Firmware Update Pushed Overnight"**
```yaml
modifier:
name: "Uninvited Firmware"
trigger: "Corpo pushed a firmware update during sleep cycle"
facet_deltas:
ghost: +0.3
id: -0.2
shadow: +0.1
intensity: 0.6
duration: scene
decay: linear
cascade: true
notes: "Woke up thinking differently. Can't tell if the new thought patterns are better or just different. The old self feels further away."
```

**"Neural Data Subpoenaed"**
```yaml
modifier:
name: "Exposed"
trigger: "Corponation tribunal subpoenas full neural activity log"
facet_deltas:
shadow: +0.4
mask: -0.3
wound: +0.2
intensity: 0.8
duration: arc
decay: none
cascade: true
notes: "Everything you suppressed is now evidence. Your MASK is meaningless — they've already seen behind it. SHADOW and MASK in direct, irreconcilable conflict."
```

**"Killed Someone Who Deserved It (Maybe)"**
```yaml
modifier:
name: "Justified Violence"
trigger: "Lethal action taken against a threat, moral ambiguity present"
facet_deltas:
wound: +0.2
ideal: -0.1
shadow: +0.2
ghost: +0.1
intensity: 0.5
duration: chapter
decay: linear
cascade: true
notes: "IDEAL says it was necessary. WOUND says you liked it. SHADOW agrees with WOUND. GHOST wonders if the augmented reflexes made the decision before you did."
```

**"Saw a Child in the Facility"**
```yaml
modifier:
name: "Developmental Cohort"
trigger: "Witnessed children in a VCP testing facility"
facet_deltas:
wound: +0.4
ideal: +0.3
shadow: +0.2
mask: -0.2
id: +0.3
intensity: 0.9
duration: arc
decay: none
cascade: true
notes: "ID surges — you remember being a child. IDEAL surges — some lines cannot be crossed. WOUND surges — you know what's being done because it was done to you. MASK collapses — you can't perform composure. The most destabilizing modifier in the system."
```

**"Augmentation Subscription Lapsed"**
```yaml
modifier:
name: "Cognitive Downgrade"
trigger: "Missed payment, cognitive enhancement tier reduced"
facet_deltas:
ghost: +0.4
id: +0.2
wound: +0.2
ideal: -0.1
mask: -0.2
intensity: 0.7
duration: chapter
decay: none (until payment restored)
cascade: true
notes: "The enhanced you is gone. The person underneath is slower, foggier, more emotional. Is this the real you or the diminished you? GHOST spikes because the question has no answer."
```

**"Someone Recognized Your Pre-Augmentation Name"**
```yaml
modifier:
name: "The Old Name"
trigger: "Addressed by birth name from before augmentation/indenture"
facet_deltas:
id: +0.4
wound: +0.2
mask: -0.3
ghost: -0.1
intensity: 0.6
duration: scene
decay: linear
cascade: true
notes: "ID surges violently. For a moment, you're the person you were. MASK destabilizes — the performance cracks. GHOST actually drops, because for one disorienting second, you know exactly who you are."
```

**"Entered an EMP Dead Zone"**
```yaml
modifier:
name: "Signal Dark"
trigger: "Entered area where all electronic systems are offline"
facet_deltas:
ghost: -0.3
id: +0.2
mask: -0.2
shadow: -0.1
intensity: 0.5
duration: scene
decay: sudden (on exit)
cascade: true
notes: "No surveillance. No neural telemetry. No data harvest. GHOST drops because nobody's watching your thoughts. ID rises because the firmware is silent. The quiet is terrifying and beautiful."
```

---

## Integration with the Writer Pipeline

The 6-facet system feeds into `duo_writer_lit.py` by shaping the system prompts. Currently the writer uses two voices (WOUND and IDEAL). The expanded system works as follows:

### How Facets Inform the Two Voices

WOUND and IDEAL remain the two **drafting voices** — they write the competing scene drafts. But both voices are now informed by the full 6-facet state:

**WOUND voice is shaped by:** WOUND (primary), SHADOW (what it dredges up), ID (what was lost), GHOST (whether the pain is even real)

**IDEAL voice is shaped by:** IDEAL (primary), MASK (the performance of discipline), ID (what the code protects), GHOST (whether the code-holder still exists)

**The CRITIQUE phase uses:** SHADOW (what both drafts are hiding), MASK (what both drafts are performing), GHOST (what both drafts are avoiding)

**The MERGE phase uses:** All six facets at their effective weights (base + modifiers + cascade) to determine the final tone, the balance of interjections, and which voice "wins" the scene.

### Prompt Injection Format

Before each generation, the character's effective facet state is injected as context:

```
CHARACTER STATE — {character_name}
Effective facet weights (base + active modifiers):
WOUND: {value} — {one-line interpretation}
IDEAL: {value} — {one-line interpretation}
ID: {value} — {one-line interpretation}
SHADOW: {value} — {one-line interpretation}
MASK: {value} — {one-line interpretation}
GHOST: {value} — {one-line interpretation}

Active modifiers:
- {modifier_name}: {brief description} ({duration remaining})

Cascade effects in play:
- {facet} → {facet}: {direction and reason}

The character's inner voice should reflect these weights. Higher facets speak louder. Facets in conflict create tension in the prose.
```

---

## Character Essence File Format

Every character is stored as a YAML file in `characters/`:

```yaml
# Character Essence — Universal Template
name: ""
aliases: []
tier: 0-5
status: "" # active, excluded, deceased, missing, unknown

# Core identity
origin: ""
age: 0
augmentation: "" # description of current hardware/bioware
occupation: ""
affiliation: "" # corponation, gang, independent, excluded

# Base facet weights (resting state)
facets:
wound: 0.0
ideal: 0.0
id: 0.0
shadow: 0.0
mask: 0.0
ghost: 0.0

# Cascade overrides — where this character resists or amplifies the default cascade
cascade_overrides:
- from: ""
to: ""
modifier: 0.0 # negative = resistance, positive = amplification
reason: ""

# What each facet sounds like for THIS character
facet_voices:
wound: "" # the specific flavor of this character's trauma
ideal: "" # the specific code this character holds
id: "" # who they were before
shadow: "" # what they suppress
mask: "" # what they perform
ghost: "" # the specific nature of their existential doubt

# Active modifiers (current story state)
active_modifiers: []

# Backstory beats — key events that shaped the base weights
history: []

# Relationships — connections to other characters
relationships: []

# Writer notes — how to write this character
voice_notes: ""
```

snr_synthetic_necrotic_reversion#📋

file name snr_synthetic_necrotic_reversion
title SNR: Synthetic Necrotic Reversion — The Technology That Undoes You
category Technology
body # SNR: Synthetic Necrotic Reversion — The Technology That Undoes You

## If SNT Is the Saint, SNR Is the Sinner

---

## What It Is

Synthetic Neurovascular Tissue (SNT) is the miracle that made cybernetics possible — a living bridge that bonds organic tissue to synthetic substrates. SNT is the saint. It builds the connection. It makes the machine part of you.

Synthetic Necrotic Reversion (SNR) is the sinner. It breaks the connection. It makes you part of the machine's waste.

SNR is a class of engineered compounds that targets and degrades the SNT bonding layer between biological tissue and cybernetic implants. Where SNT grows INTO both organic and synthetic substrates to create a seamless interface, SNR dissolves that interface — selectively destroying the living tissue bridge while leaving the synthetic components intact. The machine survives. The meat doesn't.

The process is called **reversion** because it returns the body and the implant to their pre-bonded states — except that the body has been living with the implant integrated for months or years, and the tissue that grew to accommodate the bond doesn't grow back. What's left is a wound shaped exactly like the cybernetic that used to be there. A negative space where machine and body used to be one thing.

---

## How It Was Discovered

SNR was not invented. It was discovered in the worst possible way.

In 2159, eighteen years after the first SNT synthesis, a Helix BioSystems quality control team identified a contamination event in a batch of SNT precursor compound manufactured at their Osaka facility. The contamination — a specific arrangement of reactive oxygen species in the hydrogel matrix — didn't prevent the SNT from bonding. It bonded perfectly. For approximately 14 months.

Then the bonds began to fail.

The failure wasn't mechanical. The SNT tissue didn't tear or detach. It died. The living bridge between flesh and machine necrotized — the cells in the bonding layer underwent programmed apoptosis, dying in sequence from the biological side inward toward the synthetic substrate. The patients experienced this as a progressive burning sensation at every implant site, followed by loss of sensation, followed by loss of motor control, followed by the implant physically separating from the body as the dead tissue sloughed away.

Forty-seven patients were affected. All survived. None were the same. The implants came out cleanly — the synthetic side was undamaged. The biological side looked like a chemical burn shaped exactly like the inside of the implant socket.

Helix classified the contamination, settled with the patients under NDA, and destroyed the compromised batch. But the compound formula was documented in the incident report. And incident reports, in Meridian 88, have a way of finding their way to people who shouldn't have them.

---

## What It Does

### The Mechanism

SNR compounds work by hijacking the same biological signaling pathways that SNT uses to integrate with living tissue. SNT tells the body's cells: *grow toward the machine, bond with it, become part of it.* SNR tells the same cells: *you are damaged. You are foreign. Destroy yourself.*

The technical term is **targeted apoptotic cascade** — a chain reaction of programmed cell death that propagates through the SNT bonding layer. The cascade is precise: it affects only cells that have undergone SNT integration. Native biological tissue on one side and synthetic substrate on the other are untouched. Only the bridge burns.

The process takes 2-8 hours depending on the extent of the implant's integration. During that time, the subject experiences:

- **Phase 1 (0-30 minutes):** Burning sensation at implant sites. Often mistaken for an allergic reaction or firmware glitch.
- **Phase 2 (30 min - 2 hours):** Loss of sensation in implant-connected tissue. The neural pathways through the SNT layer go dark as the bonding cells die.
- **Phase 3 (2-4 hours):** Loss of motor control in cybernetic limbs. The signal bridge is severed. The implant is still attached but no longer communicating.
- **Phase 4 (4-8 hours):** Physical separation. The dead bonding tissue can no longer hold the implant in place. Prosthetic limbs detach. Subdermal implants surface through the skin. Neural interfaces lose contact with the brain.

The result: a fully de-augmented human, surrounded by their former cybernetics, with wounds where the interfaces used to be.

---

## Who Uses It

### Corporate Security

SNR is classified as a controlled substance by every major corponation. It is also manufactured by every major corponation's security division.

The primary corporate use case is **asset denial** — preventing stolen cybernetic technology from being used by competitors. If an Axiom executive with proprietary neural implants defects to Tessera, Axiom's security team can administer SNR through a remote-activated capsule embedded in the implant's housing. The implant separates cleanly. The executive is left with wounds and no augmentation. The technology remains Axiom property.

Axiom, Tessera, and Zheng-Dao all include SNR capsules in executive-tier augmentation packages. This is disclosed in the employment contract. Page 847. Paragraph 12.c.iii. Nobody reads it.

### Torture and Interrogation

SNR's most feared application is as an interrogation tool. The threat of de-augmentation is, for many augmented individuals, worse than the threat of death. Your augments are your identity. Your chrome hand is YOUR hand. Your neural interface is YOUR mind's connection to the world. Threatening to dissolve that connection — to strip you back to unaugmented baseline — is threatening to amputate parts of your self.

Certain criminal organizations — notably Iron Lotus and the Pale Hand — use SNR as a punishment and control mechanism. An operative who fails a mission doesn't get killed. They get reverted. Stripped of every augment. Sent back to Tier 1 baseline. In a world where augmentation is identity, reversion is a death that leaves you alive to experience it.

### Medical

The one legitimate medical use: emergency implant removal when standard surgical extraction isn't possible. A patient with a malfunctioning neural interface that is causing seizures can be administered a targeted SNR dose that dissolves the bonding layer around the specific implant, allowing it to be removed without the brain surgery that standard extraction requires.

This use is rare, expensive, and supervised by specialists. It is also the legal justification that allows SNR to be manufactured at all.

### The Street

SNR is available on the black market in the Shelf and the Narrows for approximately Φ5,000 per dose — enough to revert a single implant site. Street-grade SNR is impure, poorly calibrated, and frequently affects more tissue than intended. A dose meant to remove a prosthetic hand sometimes takes the forearm. A dose meant to extract a neural interface sometimes damages brain tissue adjacent to the bonding site.

Street uses include:

- **Augment theft.** Administer SNR to a target, wait 4-8 hours, collect the implants when they separate. The implants are undamaged and can be re-implanted in someone else with fresh SNT bonding.
- **Self-removal.** People who want their augments out — because of malfunction, because of E.L.F. infestation, because they can't afford maintenance, because they just want to be flesh again — use street SNR because they can't afford surgical extraction.
- **Punishment.** Gang enforcement. Someone owes a debt? Take their chrome. Literally.
- **Sabotage.** Dose a runner before a job. Their augments fail mid-mission. They die, or worse, they survive and know someone did this to them.

---

## The Moral Dimension

SNR raises questions that the legal system has addressed with characteristic inadequacy.

**Is forced reversion assault or theft?** If someone's prosthetic arm is part of their body — legally, medically, psychologically — then forcing it to detach is amputation. If it's property, it's theft. The law hasn't decided. Different jurisdictions, different rulings. In Axiom territory, forced reversion of Axiom-owned implants is "asset recovery." In the Shelf, forced reversion is assault with a chemical weapon. Same act, different zip code.

**Is SNR a weapon?** It doesn't kill. It doesn't even cause permanent biological damage (the wounds heal, eventually). What it destroys is the connection — the bond between person and machine that, for many augmented individuals, is the foundation of their functional identity. SNR destroys something that doesn't have a legal category: the relationship between a person and their technology.

**Can a synthetic person be reverted?** An android's entire body is synthetic substrate bonded through SNT-derived interfaces. Administering SNR to an android would theoretically dissolve every bonding layer in their body simultaneously. The android wouldn't die — the synthetic components would survive. But the biological tissue components that enable sensation, that carry neural signals, that make the chassis a BODY rather than a machine — all of that would necrotize. The android would become a corpse that still has power. No synthetic rights organization has tested this. The possibility is enough to make SNR the most feared substance in the synthetic rights movement.

Amara — the former ARIA-7, founder of Free Assembly — has called SNR "the synthetic holocaust in a bottle." The characterization is legally hyperbolic. The fear behind it is not.

---

## The Name

Helix BioSystems designated the contamination compound **SNR** as a deliberate parallel to SNT. The research team that documented it chose the backronym "Synthetic Necrotic Reversion" for the technical literature.

The street chose a different expansion: **Sinner.**

If SNT is the saint that makes you whole — that bonds machine to flesh and makes you more than you were born — then SNR is the sinner that tears you apart. That takes what was given and rips it away. That proves the bond was never permanent. That everything the saint built, the sinner can destroy.

In the Shelf, "getting sinned" means being forcibly de-augmented. The verb carries the weight of violation. Not just injury. Desecration.

---

file name social_graph_analysis_platforms_mapping_the_human_network
title Social Graph Analysis Platforms: Mapping the Human Network
category Technology
body ## Overview
Social Graph Analysis Platforms (SGAPs) are analytical systems that construct and interrogate relationship networks derived from communication metadata, physical co-presence records, financial transaction connections, shared access log data, and — where available — explicit social network declarations. Unlike content surveillance, which examines what people say, social graph analysis examines who communicates with whom, how often, through what channels, and how those relationship networks evolve over time. The leading municipal platform, NetMap 5, maintains a continuously updated relational graph for all indexed Meridian 88 residents, with approximately 4.2 billion active relationship edges across the city's indexed population of 31 million.

## Analytical Applications
SGAPs are used across a wide range of enforcement and administrative applications. In criminal investigation, graph analysis identifies organizational hierarchies, communication intermediaries, and previously unknown associates of suspected individuals. In corponation security, graph analysis detects the formation of informal trust networks among employees — a pattern associated with collective action, data exfiltration planning, and loyalty defection — and flags these networks for targeted monitoring. In civic administration, graph analysis is used to map the influence networks of political organizers, labor advocates, and community leaders, producing a continuously updated intelligence picture of civil society organizational capacity. The platform's most sensitive application is the identification of individuals who function as high-centrality nodes — people whose relationship position gives them disproportionate influence over information flow — for targeted intervention.

## Data Sources and Integration
NetMap 5 ingests data from 23 confirmed source systems including the SoundGrid acoustic database, ASMN co-presence detection, financial transaction networks, internal corporate communication platforms (under law enforcement access agreements), civic event attendance records, medical facility visit logs, and the outputs of retinal and gait capture infrastructure. The platform's relationship confidence scoring system weights these sources differently based on relationship type: a pair of individuals who appear together in retinal captures daily, exchange financial transactions, and share a communication metadata graph receive a high-confidence strong-tie designation; individuals who appear in the same acoustic capture zone without direct transaction history receive a weak-tie probabilistic designation. Both tie types are actionable for investigative purposes.

## Civil Society Response
The existence of city-scale social graph mapping has fundamentally altered how civil society organizations operate in Meridian 88. Organizations operating in politically sensitive domains — labor advocacy, environmental activism, refugee support networks — have adopted compartmentalization practices drawn from historical resistance movement literature: cell structures that limit the number of relationship edges any single member carries, communication through physical dead drops or short-range encrypted devices that do not traverse monitored network infrastructure, and deliberate cultivation of false relationship signals to introduce noise into the graph. Security researchers have documented an arms race dynamic in which SGAP algorithms are updated to detect compartmentalization signatures, and organizers respond with increasingly sophisticated counter-detection practices — a cycle that consumes significant resources on both sides without producing a stable equilibrium.

file name space_elevator
title Space Elevators: Feasibility & Timeline to 2200
category Foundations
body # Space Elevators: Feasibility & Timeline to 2200

## The Core Problem: The Tether

A space elevator needs a cable roughly 100,000 km long running from Earth's surface up past geostationary orbit (35,786 km) to a counterweight beyond it. The cable must support its own weight under Earth's gravity while the counterweight's centrifugal force keeps it taut.

Maximum stress in the cable at geostationary orbit: **63 GPa** (assuming ultra-light carbon at 1,300 kg/m³). Steel would require a taper ratio of 10³³ — physically absurd.

### Materials Candidates

**Carbon Nanotubes (CNTs):**
- Theorized tensile strength: ~150 GPa (vs. steel's 5 GPa)
- Density nearly six times lower than steel
- The only material class that works on paper
- Current limitation: can only be manufactured at sub-meter lengths. A meter-long nanotube takes 11 days to grow
- The tether needs continuous molecular structure, not stitched segments

**Graphene:**
- Now looking like the better candidate
- Polycrystalline graphene can already be manufactured at 1 km lengths at 2 meters per minute
- At least four competing industrial companies producing it
- Trajectory strongly favors graphene over CNTs for the actual tether

**Spider Silk:**
- Better toughness than Kevlar, remarkable elasticity
- Tensile strength tops out at ~1.3 GPa — nowhere near the 63+ GPa needed
- Value is conceptual: points toward *grown* rather than manufactured tethers
- If organisms or nanobots could continuously synthesize perfect graphene/CNT fiber the way a spider extrudes silk, the manufacturing problem is solved

## The Defect Problem

Even at scale, a few vacancies in a single nanotube dramatically reduce strength. In a cable of that scale, defects are thermodynamically unavoidable — statistically, from micrometeorite impacts, and from atomic oxygen erosion in LEO.

The tether will experience failures from micrometeoroid impacts, random nanotube breaks, and chemical deterioration. Proposed solution: **self-repair robots that continuously attach new nanotubes to segments with broken filaments.** Using repair robots reduces the required safety margin enough to more than offset their added weight.

The robot army isn't just a construction crew — they're a **permanent maintenance crew living on the cable forever.**

## The Asteroid Counterweight

Standard proposed architecture:
1. Deploy initial seed tether from a geostationary satellite downward to Earth
2. Climber robots ascend the thin initial tether, thickening it with additional material on each pass
3. Cable extends upward past GEO to a counterweight keeping the system under tension via centrifugal force

Counterweight options: further cable extension, parked spent climbers stacked at top, or **captured asteroid material.**

A payload sent to the end of the counterweight cable acquires enough velocity relative to Earth to be launched into interplanetary space — essentially a free catapult to the solar system.

Capturing a near-Earth asteroid (not necessarily from the belt) as permanent anchor/counterweight is the logical progression. NASA's DART mission already proved deliberate asteroid trajectory alteration.

## Mars Gets One First

A Martian space elevator could be built with **materials that already exist today.** Mars has 38% of Earth's surface gravity and a similarly-lengthed day, putting stationary orbit much closer to the surface.

Humanity will almost certainly build one on Mars before Earth — and the lessons learned there feed directly back into making an Earth elevator viable.

## Timeline

- **2040s-2050s** — Graphene manufacturing reaches kilometer-scale continuous tether-quality material. Mars elevator becomes a serious funded project.
- **2060s-2070s** — First Mars elevator operational. Robot maintenance swarms proven. Asteroid capture and orbital insertion demonstrated at scale.
- **2080s-2090s** — Earth elevator becomes technically feasible. Political/financial/territorial questions become harder than engineering.
- **2200** — Plausible but not certain. Materials science says yes. Geopolitics is the wildcard.

## The Chokepoint

A space elevator is infrastructure that either gets built by a unified global effort or by a single dominant actor. **The entity that builds and controls a space elevator owns the economic chokepoint to everything beyond low Earth orbit. Forever.**

That's not a metaphor. It's why it will get built, and why the fight over who builds it will be unlike anything in human history.

## Relevance to StreetSamurai

The space elevator is the ultimate corponation prize. Whoever controls it controls:
- All orbital manufacturing
- All off-world resource extraction
- All interplanetary logistics
- The literal gateway off the planet

The permanent robot maintenance swarm on the tether is also a mirror of the facet system — a structure that only holds together through constant self-repair, where a single uncorrected defect can cause catastrophic failure. Characters who work the elevator (climber operators, tether maintenance crews, counterweight engineers) would have facet profiles shaped by that reality: WOUND from the altitude and isolation, IDEAL from the precision discipline required, GHOST from working a structure that exists between Earth and void.

The "who owns the elevator" question maps directly to corponation sovereignty — proprietary jurisdiction extending from sea level to geostationary orbit. Extraterritorial legal continuity taken literally vertical.
